title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated system producing a false match that was then acted on as though it were verified fact. The FLOCK camera read a license plate incorrectly and matched it to a different vehicle, generating an alert about a stolen plate. Officers treated that alert as sufficient grounds for a traffic stop, and the stop escalated to a K-9 deployment, an arrest, and charges. The failure sits at the handoff between an automated identification tool and the human decision to act on its output, where no independent check of the plate appears to have occurred before the stop.

What would have caught it is a verification step between the alert and the enforcement action, such as a human confirming the plate against the vehicle before initiating a stop. The reporting does not describe any such step being taken. The incident also shows that the consequences of a misread did not stay with the camera: they extended to a physical confrontation, an arrest, and charges that were later dropped.

The internal investigation found no wrongdoing in the K-9 use, and the charges were dropped according to the driver's lawyer. What disciplinary action, if any, the officers may face is not established. A camera misread is a technical error, and whether it reflects a defect in the system or its deployment conditions is not established by these reports.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Body camera footage was released showing Toledo Police officers releasing a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. Officers had received a FLOCK camera alert about a stolen license plate, but the alert was wrong because the camera misread the plate and matched it to a different vehicle. The driver, Brandon Upchurch, got out of his truck with his hands up, then walked toward the grass while officers ordered him to the ground. He was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction, and police later realized the plate information was incorrect. He received medical attention at the scene.

Multiple Toledo Police officers are under investigation over the incident. Police said they believed the driver might flee and did not know if he or a passenger had weapons. Under TPD's K-9 policy, handlers should weigh the severity of the crime, whether the suspect poses an immediate threat, and whether the suspect is resisting or trying to evade arrest before deploying the dog. The article does not say what disciplinary action, if any, the officers may face.
